reason: Strict uncertainty default: the context favors standard effect (functional efficacy), but the original HGM dngos po field itself contains have any affect, and the extant direct English witnesses retain the same intelligible functional paraphrase. That field may derive from this corpus and is not independent proof. No corrected direct witness or publication-level evidence was found. An idiosyncratic nominal use of affect for affecting is not ruled out sufficiently to send a typo claim to editors. Refutation means the defect is unestablished, not that the standard copyedit would be unreasonable.
parallel_witness: C16:799: A deed which is already gone is no longer a thing that can have any affect on anything. C05/C16 ACIP, Wylie and English are each exactly equal. ILL:1878: And a karma which has already stopped could never exist as a functioning thing; how then could the karma give forth its result? ILL ends at brtsad pa'i, omitting lan du; no independence or ingestion lineage is inferred.

a.finding: Exact found phrase is present in C05:222 English.

b.finding: C16:799 duplicates all three fields; it is not demonstrated independent publication evidence. The shorter ILL:1878 has a different functioning-thing rendering. Global searches include C16, P1 and TCS texts; no P1/TCS matching passage or corrected phrase found.

c.finding: No existing C05:222 or found-phrase record. This is not one of the already registered apparatus classes.

d.finding: Effect is a plausible standard copyedit in context, but a defensible authorial nominal use of affect for capacity to affect remains unexcluded. HGM dngos po includes functional thing and have any affect in the same original field; this is attestation, not independent grammatical validation. Under the required uncertainty default the defect remains unestablished.

e.finding: Rechecked exact have any affect on anything=2 (C05:222/C16:799), have any effect on anything=0, any affect=2, thing that can have any effect=0; Tibetan passage patterns=3 (C05:222/C16:799/ILL:1878). The zhig search limit 12 and brtsad limit 10 were reproduced as limited result sets, not total supporting attestation counts.

source_claim.evidence: C05:222 has nominal 'affect' after 'any'. Exact field comparison finds the same reading in C16:799, which establishes repetition but not an independent publication or a correction; no corpus row contains 'have any effect on anything'. The source remains unchanged pending printed-source review.
